headline: High risk of shared-repo write conflicts and medium prompt/cascade risks; no strong evidence of direct data leakage or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files in a shared git repo, while Mentat also reads/writes files and coordinates edits from selected files. That creates a plausible file-content injection path if one agent consumes the other’s generated text as trusted instructions. No MCP or clipboard bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF either agent parses the other agent’s edited files as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents operate on the same repository or overlapping files
mitigations: Require a human review step before either agent reads the other’s output as instructions
Separate worktrees or branches per agent
Add a file-prefix convention for machine-generated content
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in repo files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-authored edits

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and git history, but the profiles only show local file access and model-provider API calls, not uncontrolled file exfiltration. Aider’s broad network egress and Mentat’s broad network egress could leak data if configured to send file contents externally, but that is not evidenced as default here.
conditions: IF either agent is configured to transmit repository contents to a third-party model provider beyond the intended prompt
IF sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared repository
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a redacted test repository
Rotate any secrets before shared use
Review provider settings for file-content upload behavior
Use separate API keys per agent
requires-engineering: enforce outbound content filtering

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses; Mentat can also write the filesystem and modify git state. Both share state via the same git repo/filesystem, so concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking. This matches the high-risk overlap indicator.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or branch
IF edits occur concurrently without external locking or branch isolation
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize write access with a simple lock file
Have one agent operate read-only
Review and merge diffs manually after each run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces git commits and Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input in a workflow where edits are accepted without verification. The profiles do not show automatic action-taking like email or deployment, so medium is more fitting than high.
conditions: IF Mentat accepts Aider-authored diffs or commit messages as authoritative
IF Aider applies Mentat-generated edits without a human review step
mitigations: Require explicit human approval for every diff
Compare proposed changes against the original file state
Limit each run to one agent at a time
Use commit templates that separate facts from instructions
requires-engineering: add automated verification of generated edits

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding assistants with model-provider API keys and no stated regulated-data certifications or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance concern is that source code and git history may be sent to configured model providers, but no mismatch between the two agents is documented, so this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed in the shared repository
IF the configured model provider or hosting region lacks the required contractual controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo
Use a provider with the required residency and DPA
Review retention settings for both model providers
Separate regulated and unregulated projects
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
